messages:
Anya (PM): Hey team — dropping the Figma for the first-run flow I iterated on. Main pieces: a compact setup checklist modal + a persistent quickstart banner with sample projects carousel. Looking for quick UX + a11y scan. https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/redwood-first-run Oliver (Design): Nice! high-level: I prefer the persistent banner for power users, but mobile needs a tighter layout. Quick note: the banner blue on white feels low contrast at small sizes. Maria (Product): We should include a clear 'Save progress' state. If a user dismisses the banner we need a way to restore it from the account menu. Also want analytics hooks for which sample project is selected. Sam T. (Frontend): Quick implementation notes: banner can be a role="region" with aria-label="Quickstart banner". For the carousel I'll wire data-analytics: `\{"event\":\"onboarding_sample_select\",\"sample\":\"\"\}` Luke (Accessibility): Contrast: the light blue cta on white fails WCAG for normal text. Suggest swapping to the darker 500 token or adding a 1px border and stronger shadow. Keyboard: ensure banner tab order is logical and the carousel has visible focus styles. Also need `aria-live="polite"` announcements when progress updates. Oliver (Design): Microcopy: header currently "Welcome to Redwood — let's get you set up" is wordy. Options: "Get started" or "Set up in minutes". CTA variants: A) "Start with sample project" B) "Create your first project" — lean A for lower friction. Anya (PM): Good calls. We should A/B test CTAs and banner persistence: variant A = sticky banner, variant B = inline helper that appears under the header. Track click-through + completion of setup checklist. Sam T. (Frontend): Accessibility nit: when hiding the banner we must move keyboard focus, e.g., focus the next logical element or a toast with an undo. Also implement `prefers-reduced-motion` for carousel transitions. Maria (Product): UX detail: checklist should be resumable and show a small progress chip in the top-right of the console (so users don't rely on the banner). Progress chip should be keyboard reachable. Luke (Accessibility): Screen reader flow: reading order must be modal -> checklist -> main content. Avoid reordering DOM just for visual layout. For dismissible elements add `aria-controls` pointing to the restored area. Oliver (Design): Visual tweak idea: compress sample project cards to two rows on desktop instead of full-width carousel to reduce cognitive load. Also add subtle tag badges like "Demo", "Internal" to set expectations. Anya (PM): Can we make the sample projects explicit about their latency/cost tradeoffs? tiny label: "Low cost demo" or "Production-ready". Maria — do we have data to map binaries? Maria (Product): We can add a metadata field to samples. We'll surface `cost_hint` and `recommended_env` in the card. Sam T. (Frontend): Implementation snippet for banner container: ```
``` Make sure dismiss action sets `aria-hidden=true` and moves focus. Luke (Accessibility): Avoid using `display:none` immediately for focusable dismiss; move focus first, then hide. Also provide `aria-live` update: "Setup progress saved" when a step completes. Oliver (Design): Copy tweak suggestions inline: header -> "Get started with Redwood"; step titles 1–3 short verbs: "Create", "Connect", "Test". CTA compact: "Start demo". Anya (PM): Scheduling: let's do a 20-min usability check with 3 engineers on Tue 2pm. Also roll a staging preview so folks can click around. ci-bot: Preview deployed: https://staging.redwood.internal/onboarding?exp=first-run-compact-2026 (flag: onboarding_compact_v2) :rocket: Maria (Product): I'll add analytics mapping + GA events: `onboarding.banner_shown`, `onboarding.sample_clicked`, `onboarding.checklist_completed`. Sam T. (Frontend): I'll pick up the accessibility fixes and reduced-motion next. I'll add keyboard tests to the e2e suite. Luke (Accessibility): quick checklist for PR: contrast check, focus outline present, aria-live messages, keyboard tab order verified, screen reader walkthrough. I'll review the PR before merge. :a11y: Oliver (Design): LGTM, small follow-ups on spacing and mobile stacking. I'll push an updated figma by EOD. :+1: Anya (PM): Amazing — thanks all. If nobody objects, I'll ship the A/B test config and schedule the usability session. Maria (Product): No objections. :eyes: Anya (PM): ok moving forward then, tagging the rollout plan in the docs channel after staging feedback.
